# 1.27.0 — instructions, a quicker new chat, calmer model tooltips

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## Instructions

A new page, **Settings → Instructions**, keeps your own know-how for particular topics. Each
instruction has a name, a few trigger words and the text itself.

- In a chat the model sees only the list: names and trigger words, never the texts. It is told to
  open an instruction whenever your message touches its topic, before doing anything else, and to
  follow it while solving the task. Matching is the model's own judgement: letter case and language
  don't matter, and related wording counts — the trigger words are hints, not exact keys.
- The answer shows which instruction it used: a small **Instruction** mark above the reply. Click
  it to open the instruction in Settings.
- An instruction can be switched off without deleting it: the model then no longer sees it.
- Instructions are plain Markdown files in the profile's `instructions` folder. They can be
  exported to a `.md` file and imported back, one or several at once. A `.md` file dropped into
  the folder by hand is picked up too; its file name becomes the instruction's name.
- Trigger words are entered as tags: Enter or a comma adds one, pasting a comma-separated list adds
  them all, repeats are ignored.
- Instructions travel in the data archive together with the settings, and each profile has its own.

Only the chat model reads instructions. When it hands a job to the agent, it passes on whatever
the agent needs from them.

## Smaller changes

- Clicking the app logo at the top of the open sidebar now starts a new chat. On the folded
  sidebar it still unfolds it.
- Tooltips in the model picker no longer pop up the moment the pointer passes over a row, and no
  longer cover the list: they wait a moment and appear beside the picker.
- The window is now an ordinary application window for Windows. Before, it was registered as a
  tool window: its taskbar button sometimes appeared only after the window was first focused, it
  was missing from Alt+Tab, and minimizing another program could take it down too.

## File

`Amarin-Admin-AI-v1.27.0-win-x64.exe` — a single file, nothing to unpack.
